turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The preachers… they speak with such conviction, don't they? It is unsettling to hear such certainty about matters beyond my understanding, Nikhil.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My concern is not with the source of fear, Sandip, but with the disruption of order. I will not engage in speculation regarding my motives, nor will I tolerate accusations leveled against me or my household. Let us be clear: my request for you to depart my lands stands.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Such certainty… it can be quite isolating, wouldn’t you agree, Nikhil? It makes one feel… adrift, when one’s own convictions are less defined.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Isolating, you say, my dear Bimala? Perhaps it is the burden of *knowing*, the weight of responsibility, that separates one from the comforting currents of popular opinion. And as for your… request, Nikhil, it strikes me as remarkably similar to the pronouncements of Nero, condemning the Christians to the lions, all while feigning concern for their well-being.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies, Sandip, are predictably extravagant and entirely irrelevant. I am not concerned with historical comparisons, but with the present reality – your continued presence on my land is unwelcome. I trust you understand the implications of further defiance.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Implications, you say? My dear Nikhil, I am merely observing the trajectory of events, charting the predictable tides of consequence. One might even say, I am a Cassandra, burdened with foresight that no one wishes to heed, and destined to watch the impending storm gather on your horizon.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Cassandra… a rather dramatic choice, isn't it, Sandip? I find myself wondering if such pronouncements serve a purpose beyond merely unsettling the air between us.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Unsettling the air, you say, Bimala? Surely, a little turbulence is necessary to stir the stagnant waters of complacency. And as for your… *implications*, Nikhil, I find your veiled threats rather amusing. Do you truly believe a few harsh words can silence the whispers of discontent that ripple through this province?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A Cassandra, you claim? It seems a heavy mantle for one so young to bear, Sandip. Tell me, does this foresight also extend to predicting the consequences of such theatrical pronouncements?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Consequences, my dear Bimala? Why, they are as inevitable as the monsoon, though perhaps less refreshing. You inquire about my foresight? Let us simply say I observe patterns, and I see a rather…uncomfortable one emerging, particularly concerning the fervor of those preachers from the north – a fervor that finds fertile ground in dissatisfaction, wouldn’t you agree, Nikhil?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The preachers… their influence is undeniable, Sandip, though I find your insistence on linking it so directly to Nikhil’s standing rather… pointed. Do you truly believe their words hold such power, or are you merely seeking a convenient scapegoat for the unrest you seem so eager to cultivate?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A convenient scapegoat? My dear Bimala, you wound me with your cynicism! I merely observe, as a diligent scholar of human affairs would, that discontent, like a vine, requires a trellis to climb. And who, pray tell, provides a more convenient trellis than a charismatic, albeit misguided, religious figure?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your analogies are needlessly dramatic, Sandip. I am not concerned with the metaphorical trellises you perceive, but with the tangible well-being of my tenants and the stability of this region. Let us speak plainly: if your observations are as astute as you claim, you should direct your counsel toward mitigating the preachers' influence, rather than exploiting it.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Mitigating their influence? My dear Nikhil, you mistake me. I am not an engineer constructing dams, but a cartographer charting the course of a river – one that, I suspect, is about to flood its banks. And concerning the well-being of your tenants… one wonders, doesn’t one, if a certain… paternalistic approach isn’t itself contributing to the very dissatisfaction I observe?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A cartographer, you say? It seems you find a certain… satisfaction in predicting storms, Sandip. But tell me, does charting a river's course truly offer any solace to those swept away by its flood?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Solace, my dear Bimala, is a luxury afforded to those who build their houses on solid ground. I suspect your husband’s tenants find themselves rather closer to the riverbank, wouldn't you agree, Nikhil? A little… instability, a little… questioning of the established order, can be quite invigorating, don't you think?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Invigorating, you suggest? Perhaps it is invigorating to observe chaos, Sandip, but I confess I find little pleasure in the prospect of upheaval for those who have so little to begin with. Surely, a true leader seeks to build, not simply to watch the river erode the foundations.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric, Sandip, is tiresome. I understand you enjoy presenting yourself as a keen observer, but your pronouncements are increasingly devoid of substance and designed to sow discord. I will not entertain further insinuations regarding my management of the estate or my tenants' contentment.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, but 'substance,' Nikhil, is often what one *perceives* it to be, isn't it? Like a mirage shimmering on the horizon – tantalizing, perhaps, but ultimately illusory. I merely point out the shifting sands beneath your feet; it’s your prerogative to ignore them, of course, though I daresay the river has a way of reminding us all of its power.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: A mirage, you say? How easily you dismiss what you choose not to see, Sandip. I wonder, though, if it is the mirage itself that deceives, or the thirst that compels one to pursue it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
